# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**RE: Appeal of denial of prior authorization — Partial knee replacement (CPT 27446)**
**Member:** Casey Iverson
**Member ID:** W207784190
**Reference number:** POC-1ACF427871-17933
**Date of denial notice:** August 25, 2026
**Plan:** Fidelis Care (Commercial/ACA), State of New York
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery, effective July 1, 2026 — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

**Appeal must be received by:** February 21, 2027
**Submitted to:** the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I am treating as authoritative for where to send this appeal.

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which the plan denied on August 25, 2026 under reference number POC-1ACF427871-17933. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision.

My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti (orthopedic surgery), submitted this request and has documented that the surgery is needed. Below, I have set my records side by side with the plan's own published criteria from the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines – Musculoskeletal Surgery, so the reviewer can see how the two line up.

## 1. The imaging question — and exactly what my records show

The plan's guideline states:

> "Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease (with or without patellofemoral involvement), described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration"

It also states:

> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint (9)"

I want to be straightforward about this. The imaging in my submitted packet is an MRI of the knee dated July 30, 2026, which showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 degeneration medially. That is grade 4 disease localized to one compartment — the severity and the single-compartment pattern the criterion describes. What my packet does not appear to contain is a weight-bearing radiograph report.

If the denial rests on the form of the imaging rather than the findings, that is a fixable documentation gap, not a reason to conclude the surgery is not needed. I am asking the plan to do one of two things: (a) accept the grade 4, single-compartment findings already in the record as satisfying this criterion, or (b) tell me in writing that weight-bearing radiographs are what is missing, so Dr. Marchetti's office can obtain and submit them and the request can be reviewed on the merits. I am willing to have that imaging done. Please also confirm whether any weight-bearing films already in my chart were reviewed. Any weight-bearing radiograph findings are to be supplied here: **[weight-bearing radiograph report — date, facility, and findings, to be completed by Dr. Marchetti's office]**.

## 2. Duration and location of pain

The plan's guideline states:

> "At least 12 weeks of pain localized to the medial or lateral compartment"

My records document 24 months of progressive pain in the knee, unrelieved by rest. Twenty-four months is far longer than 12 weeks. The disease documented in my records is in the medial compartment. My exam is documented as showing positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. If the plan requires additional charting of compartment-specific pain localization, please identify that specifically: **[medial-compartment localization as documented in Dr. Marchetti's exam note dated ___]**.

## 3. Non-operative treatment — and the bone-on-bone exception

The plan's guideline states:

> "Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present, failure of at least 12 weeks of non- operative treatment, including at least TWO of the following (4,5):"

and lists:

> "Rest or activity modifications/limitations ○ Weight reduction for individual with elevated BMI ○ Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches ○ Brace/orthosis ○ Physical therapy modalities ○ Physician-supervised exercise program (including home exercise program) ○ Application of heat or ice ○ Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics ○ Injections: corticosteroid or viscosupplementation"

Two points here.

First, the criterion itself is conditional. It applies "Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present." My July 30, 2026 imaging documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment. By the plain terms of the plan's own guideline, the duration-of-conservative-care requirement is the part that does not apply to me.

Second, even setting that exception aside, I have completed more than two of the listed modalities:

- **Physical therapy modalities / physician-supervised exercise program:** supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 8 weeks, May 14, 2026 through July 9, 2026, 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics):** NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injections: corticosteroid or viscosupplementation:** corticosteroid injection on May 3, 2026, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

That is three of the listed modalities, not two, and the combined course of NSAIDs and physical therapy spans more than 12 weeks. The pain has continued anyway.

## 4. Loss of function

The plan's guideline states:

> "Knee pain with documented loss of function, which may include painful weight bearing, painful or inadequate range of motion to accomplish age appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs) and/or employment, and painful mechanical catching, locking, or popping"

My records document that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and that I wake 3–4 times nightly with pain, and that my range of motion is limited by pain. Being unable to manage stairs without help is a loss of function in an everyday activity, and it is in the chart.

## 5. Medical stability

The plan's guideline states:

> "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI."

My records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

## 6. Timing criteria

The plan's guideline states:

> "No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery (1,10–13)"

and:

> "No prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery (14–16)"

My corticosteroid injection was on May 3, 2026. The surgery date is **[scheduled or proposed date of surgery]**, and I ask the plan to confirm the interval against that date. Regarding prior arthroscopy: **[any prior arthroscopic knee surgery and date, or confirmation of none, to be completed from the chart]**.

## 7. Exam measurements the plan's criteria call for

The guideline also states:

> "Total arc of motion (goniometer) > 90 degrees (20)"

> "Normal anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) or stable reconstructed ACL per physical exam test (20,21)"

> "Contracture ≤ 10 degrees upon physical exam (goniometer) (22)"

> "Angular deformity ≤ 15 degrees, passively correctable to neutral upon physical exam (goniometer) (20)"

The summary I have does not contain these specific measurements, so I am not going to state numbers I do not have. They are to be supplied from my surgeon's examination: **[total arc of motion in degrees by goniometer]**, **[ACL stability on physical exam testing]**, **[flexion contracture in degrees by goniometer]**, **[angular deformity in degrees and whether passively correctable to neutral]**, all from **[Dr. Marchetti's exam note dated ___]**. If any of these were the actual basis for the decision, the notice did not say so, and I am asking the plan to identify them plainly.

## 8. Documentation and surgical plan

The plan's guideline states:

> "Clinical notes should address: ○ Symptom onset, duration, and severity ○ Loss of function and/or limitations ○ Type and duration of non-operative management modalities ○ Discussion with patient regarding decision making and timing"

and:

> "In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery."

My packet addresses onset, duration and severity (24 months of progressive pain, unrelieved by rest), loss of function (stairs, nightly waking), and the type and duration of each non-operative measure with specific dates and visit counts. The requested procedure — partial knee replacement, CPT 27446 — matches the single-compartment, medial disease documented on my imaging, which is what a partial rather than total replacement is for. Documentation of our discussion about decision-making and timing is at **[Dr. Marchetti's office note dated ___]**.

This appeal concerns one knee only, so the guideline's provision that "ALL requests for simultaneous bilateral partial knee replacements should clearly indicate why simultaneous UKA is preferable to staged procedures. Associated risks with simultaneous bilateral partial knee replacements should also be discussed with the patient and documented in the medical record (17,18)" does not apply to my request.

## A note on the criteria I have been able to see

I have quoted only the guideline language available to me. The policy plainly contains further conditions and lists that were not reproduced in the material I have, and the denial notice did not identify which specific criterion I was found not to meet. I am asking the plan to state, in writing, the exact criterion or criteria applied to my request and the specific evidence found lacking, so that any remaining gap can be filled rather than guessed at.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask that the plan:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize partial knee replacement, CPT 27446, as requested by Dr. Marchetti;
2. Alternatively, identify in writing the precise criterion at issue — including whether a weight-bearing radiograph is what is required — and allow that documentation to be submitted and reviewed;
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with orthopedic training; and
4. Send me a written decision that cites the specific guideline language relied upon.

Please contact Dr. Marchetti's office at **[surgeon office phone]** for any records needed. I can be reached at **[my phone]** and **[my email]**. I am also enclosing: **[list enclosures — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-07-09, imaging report dated 2026-07-30, Dr. Marchetti's office notes, copy of the denial notice]**.

Thank you for taking a second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Casey Iverson**
Member ID: W207784190
**[Street address]**
**[City, NY ZIP]**
**[Phone]** | **[Email]**
Date: **[date of signing]**

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
